name: DWO World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The promotion's top title changed hands controversially again and again across this collection's own holdings: won, vacated by presidential decree, won again in a rematch marred by the same interference, won a year later in a battle royal, won again from a returning ex-convict in a riot that collapsed the ring, and taken one last time in the promotion's own final match.
notes: Source: DWO Wrestle Mayhem (30 Nov 1996, part 3) and DWO Holiday Bash (24 Dec 1996, parts 1 and 5).

name: DWO Eastern Championship
epitaph: Defended once cleanly and once controversially across this collection's holdings, changing hands at Holiday Bash when a returning John Jennings' interference backfired on the champion he meant to help.
notes: Source: DWO Holiday Bash (24 Dec 1996, part 2).

name: DWO National Championship
epitaph: The only title on the Holiday Bash card to survive the night unchanged, with Apollo turning back Sick Rick's steel-cage challenge in the held record's longest recorded match.
notes: Source: DWO Holiday Bash (24 Dec 1996, parts 3 and 4).

name: DWO World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Decided in a street fight through the streets of Corona, New York, with Havok's Mr. Pink and Guy Stone outlasting The Merchants of Chaos for the belts at Holiday Bash.
notes: Source: DWO Holiday Bash (24 Dec 1996, part 3).

name: DWO Women's Championship
caption: Billed vacant for years before WrestleKade X, where Tiffany won it wrestling under the ring name Phoenix.
epitaph: Vacant for years by the promotion's own account before Phoenix (Tiffany) won it in a bloody, interference-marred match against Iris Galiver at WrestleKade X.

name: DWO Final Fight Tournament
epitaph: A one-time, sixteen-man tournament run across the promotion's own last card, its final round an eight-man Thunderdome elimination match.
